title: Serve Economics: field-ready mini deck and battlecard (draft)
content:
Slide 1 — Title / Goal
- Title: Serve Economics: quick win playbook for platform and product teams (mini deck)
- One-line goal: Give AE/SE a 5-minute pitch + 10-minute demo path to prove cost/latency ROI and de-risk a pilot.
- Speaker note: use this when customer asks "How will this impact our inference bill and latency SLOs?"

Slide 2 — Positioning (how we open)
- Opening hook: Most teams pick a model, then get surprised by cost and unstable latency when usage grows.
- Quick value prop bullets: predictable SLOs, unit economics controls, same API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Talk track: "We focus on serving: keep your model choices flexible but make inference costs and reliability predictable."

Slide 3 — Common customer archetypes + pain signals
- Archetype A: AI-native startup — cares about per-request latency and token cost for scale.
- Archetype B: Mid-market product team — needs SLA and audit/data controls.
- Archetype C: Platform team — wants consistent infra across BU, cost allocations.
- Pain signals to listen for: rising token spend, cache misses, tail latency spikes, ad-hoc infra scripts.

Slide 4 — Quick ROI framework (2-min calc for meetings)
- Inputs: current tokens/mo, average response length, percentile latency SLO, infra spend on GPUs or hosted vendor line items.
- Outputs: estimated token cost reduction from batching/caching/quantization, estimated latency gain, projected payback months on Dedicated commits.
- Simple formula in talk: conservative savings = tokens/mo * 0.18 (example) — then adjust by workload type.
- Speaker tip: always capture current token volume and 95th latency before pilot

Slide 5 — Feature hooks that sell (product checklist)
- Automatic KV/prefix caching — talk about 2–5x token savings on assistant-style workflows.
- Continuous batching with latency SLOs — explain how throughput increases without hurting p95.
- Model variants & fallback routing — reliability narrative: always-on with graceful downgrade.
- Quantization & kernel selection — cost story for price-sensitive customers.

Slide 6 — Two demo flows (10-minute demo plan)
- Demo A: Hosted API quick win
  - Show baseline generation (single prompt) and tokens/latency metrics in Console.
  - Enable prefix caching and re-run scenario with repeated prompts to show tokens saved.
  - Flip to routing policy: emulate capacity pressure and show automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant.
- Demo B: Dedicated pilot (for larger customers)
  - Show committed capacity dashboard, projected monthly cost vs. pay-as-you-go, and SLA targets.
  - Run a burst test and show autoscaling/burst capacity handling.

Slide 7 — Objection handling snippets (battlecard)
- "We already have a solution in-house." -> "Great — we can complement: keep model training/internal, use Redwood for serving economics and SLA-backed uptime; we focus on operational complexity. Quick pilot can be a sidecar to your infra"
- "We can't change models" -> "You don't have to. Redwood routes and pins versions; cost and quantization recommendations are non-invasive."
- "Security/compliance concerns" -> "Private deployments (VPC, on-prem) with KMS integrations and audit logs; propose a short security review checklist."

Slide 8 — Pilot checklist (what to ask / what to collect)
- Access: API keys or network peering details for Private/Dedicated.
- Baseline metrics: tokens/day, p50/p95 latency, error rates, cost per token.
- Workload samples: representative prompt set, expected concurrency, critical failure modes.
- Success criteria: % token cost reduction target, p95 latency target, time-to-first-response SLA.

Slide 9 — One-page decision guide for execs (email-ready)
- Bullet TL;DR: "Pilot in 4 weeks — expected unit cost reduction 15–35% (workload dependent); predictable monthly commit options; enterprise controls available."
- Ask: Decide pilot scope (Hosted test vs Dedicated reserve), assign an SRE/ML eng point, and agree success metrics.
- Estimated next steps timeline: kickoff week 0, data collection week 1–2, pilot tuning week 3–4, review week 5.

Slide 10 — Pricing/commit language cheatsheet (SE-friendly)
- Hosted: pay-per-token + optional premium SLAs. Note: sample ballpark numbers for quick calc (use updated pricing sheet)
- Dedicated: commit level example calculations and how burst capacity is billed.
- Private: license + integration services estimate.
- Speaker tip: always pull the current pricing sheet link before quoting

Slide 11 — Competitive talking points (short)
- Against cloud managed endpoints: we provide tuned serving runtime + batching/quantization playbooks out of the box.
- Against single-vendor LLM APIs: we unify multi-variant routing and let customers pick tradeoffs per-route.
- Against self-hosted inference stacks: faster time-to-value and less ops burden — show how we reduce MTTD/MTTR.

Slide 12 — Playbook next steps & attachments
- Internal actions before sending to prospect: grab token volumes, check platform region, assign solution engineer, prepare demo seed prompts.
- Attachments to include with the deck: quick ROI spreadsheet, security checklist, sample contract language.

Appendix — Short scripts and soundbites
- Opening 30s: "We don't sell models. We sell predictable serving — lower costs, stable latency, and safe rollouts so your product teams can ship faster."
- 60s ROI teaser: "If you’re spending X on tokens and seeing tail latency Y, we can usually cut the unit cost by mid-teens with caching and batching, and protect p95 by smart routing."
- Closing ask: "Give us a short pilot: 4 weeks, we supply the plan and dashboards, you measure the improvement."

Notes to self (informal items to iterate)
- Swap example savings numbers with real benchmarks from internal Optimize team before next review.
- Add specific pricing links and up-to-date commit math.
- Collect 2 customer quotes for the final slide.
- TODO: make a one-slide cheat sheet for AE Slack quick post

End of deck (draft).

Document state: intentionally rough — mix of slide headings, speaker notes, quick scripts, demo checklist and objection responses for field enablement. Use this as the canonical draft for SEs to localize per-account.
